title: HCP — Hard Delete Entry — payload
description: The request payload of the HCP 2.0-draft-3 Hard delete operation (HCP 5.4.2, 5.4; `DELETE /v2/entries/{entryId}?hardDelete=true` in HCP 9.2, 9.4.5): a Management Client, acting for the Authorizing Principal, permanently removes an entry. HCP defines no schema for this operation; the members come from HCP 9.2 and 9.4.5. The outer document members (id, type, issuer, recipient, issuedAt, expiresAt, proof) are owned by the framework — SPEC §6.3. Every maxLength, maxItems and maxProperties in this schema is a Trust Tasks framework bound (SPEC §7.3 item 19), not an HCP requirement; so is every minLength or minItems of 1 on a member HCP's own schema allows to be empty.

entryId.description: HCP `entryId` (the `{entryId}` path parameter of HCP 9.2, 9.4.5): the entry's stable `id` (HCP 4.2), by which a Management Client names an entry (HCP 9.4.5).

accessToken.description: The Management Client's HCP access token (HCP 9.3), carried unchanged. HCP's HTTP binding sends it as a Bearer token; this member carries it in the document. The provider validates it exactly as over HTTP and treats it as opaque. The maxLength is a framework bound, not an HCP requirement. OPTIONAL: where it is absent, the provider authenticates the request's `issuer` VID, by the REQUIRED request proof, as a Management Client the Authorizing Principal enrolled (HCP 3.2.3), and refuses any other issuer with permissionDenied; where it is present, the token rules apply unchanged. Pending HCP confirmation (question 56).

Response.title: HCP — Hard Delete Entry — response payload
Response.description: The entry is permanently removed (HCP 5.4.2). The shape of HCP 9.4.5's withdraw result with `hardDeleted` true and no `status`, pending HCP confirmation (question 11 in the spec's "Pending HCP confirmation" section). Failures use trust-task-error, not this shape.

entryId.description: HCP `entryId`: the entry, named as the caller named it (HCP 9.4.5, 5.2.5).

hardDeleted.description: HCP `hardDeleted`: always true here, since the entry was removed, not withdrawn (HCP 9.4.5, 5.4.2).

respondedAt.description: HCP `timestamp`, renamed: the date-time of the response (HCP 9.4.5).
